item.title: Apple M5 Ultra
item.description: Apple introduced the M5 Ultra on August 25, 2026, in the new Mac Studio, built the same way as its predecessors: two M5 Max dies fused together over UltraFusion, now running at more than 4.4TB/s of inter-die bandwidth. The 80-core GPU keeps the same core count as the M3 Ultra but adds a Neural Accelerator inside every core, and Apple configures it with 96GB, 256GB, or 512GB of unified memory at up to 1.2TB/s of bandwidth, alongside a 36-core CPU and 32-core Neural Engine.

item.title: Apple M6
item.description: Apple announced the M6 on August 25, 2026, putting it in the Mac mini rather than a higher-end machine and making it the first Apple chip built on a 2nm process. The 12-core CPU pairs two of Apple’s new “super cores” with four performance cores and six efficiency cores, and the 12-core GPU adds a Neural Accelerator to every core. Apple caps unified memory at 32GB, with the entry 16GB configuration running at 153GB/s of bandwidth and upgraded configurations reaching 170GB/s.
